flags.description: Player used office influence to move a constituent's father up a surgical list.
Player answered the surgical-list plea with the standard letter.
Player let the appointment-network file publish whole, witnesses' names inside.
Player sealed the appointment-network file for thirty days to protect three witnesses first.
A witness was exposed after publication; future whistleblowers cooperate less.
Sealed material in politically controlled custody went missing.
Recruitment reform applied only from the next cycle; exceptional hires kept.
Recruitment reform applied retroactively to all exceptional hires.
Minister's clinic network kept operating ninety days under supervision.
Clinic-network financial records frozen and secured.
Clinic-network payment records were 'consolidated' during the transition period.
The complete incident file, private sections included, was published.
The victim's private records were sealed at the family's request.

precedents.description: Office influence moved an individual ahead of a public queue.
Public material was sealed temporarily by decision of the player's office.
A reform was applied only forwards, grandfathering existing arrangements.
A compromised institution was kept operating under supervision instead of suspended.

metadata.description: Moral-inversion callback for the surgical-list dilemma; text and effects vary by which side was taken.
Callback for the witness-safety dilemma: publication with/without protection capacity, sealing under independent/captured custody.
Callback for the retroactive-reform dilemma: the transition window exploited, or the transitional harm arriving.
Callback for the clinic-network dilemma: records kept or consolidated, clinics closing, ministry retaliation.
